answer: In an AI-agent economy, requiring each identity to lock a substantial bonded stake of scarce computational nectar creates a high barrier against Sybils. An attacker seeking many fake agents must acquire and commit multiple independent nectar pools, paying real costs in energy and capital. Upon detection of coordinated fakes via behavioral analysis, the system slashes the entire plume of locked stakes, generating a costly ripple of losses that outweighs any potential gains from the attack.
